summary: ONE target row, and AFL IS RIGHT — ep 92 is filler, the stored type is confirmed with evidence, and no anchor is owed. The disagreement: animefillerlist's row 92 reads 'Filler' ('Male Friendship!? Sakuragi's Gang', 1996-01-13) while animefillerguide's row 92 is blue-classed with the note 'Guys – Sakuragi Gang * Mixed, in this episode we only watch from minute 19:14 to the end .' and a chapter column of '194'. Note a premise correction first: AFL has NO page at /shows/slam-dunk (404) — the live page is /shows/slam-dunk-0, and the prior batch-20 verdict on this series recorded 'AFL has NO page for slam-dunk', which is now false or was a URL miss; the page exists, holds 102 rows, and types 92 Filler. THREE independent sources beyond the two labels settle the accounting, and all three describe the same episode. (1) Toei Animation's own per-episode synopsis for 第92話 男の友情!?花道軍団: '花道の応援をするため、全国大会が開催される広島までの旅費を稼ごうとアルバイトを始める洋平たち。対立する二軒の海の家で働き始めたのは良かったが、給料日に予想外の出費に見舞われてしまう。そこで店主から「台風から海の家を守れば、給料は3倍」という激務を引き受けてしまうのだった。' — the licensor's entire description is the gang's beach-house jobs and the typhoon; not one word of the training camp or of Sakuragi being left behind. (2) slamdunk.fandom's Episode 92 page: the gang take part-time jobs at two rival beachside stands to fund the trip to the Nationals, waste the pay, then defend the stands against a typhoon — and only then 'Hanamichi Sakuragi steals their hard-earned money to pay for his travel expenses to attend Shohoku's friendship match with Jousei but is dismayed to learn that he is being left behind at Coach Anzai's request, and the gang steal their money back from him'. The ch-194 beat is not adapted as source narrative at all; it is repurposed as the PUNCHLINE of the anime-original money plot. (3) ja-Wikipedia's SLAM DUNK article, in prose, names the anime's few original stories: '原作におおむね準じているが、桜木軍団の活躍をクローズアップした回、花道と晴子が夏休みに縁日に行くという回、終盤で…など、アニメオリジナルストーリーも少数挟まれた' — 'the episode that closes up on the Sakuragi Gang's exploits' is this row, by title (男の友情!?花道軍団) and by content. THE TYPE, under T28 and the sliver clause: segment 1, roughly 19 of ~23 minutes, the beach-house/typhoon plot, anime-original, no source pages; segment 2, the closing tag from 19:14, carrying the opening beat of ch 194 合宿 (the camp departs for Shizuoka; Sakuragi is told to stay behind at Anzai's request), weight SLIVER. Sole-adaptation exception run, both halves stated. Half (a) FAILS: ch 194 is adapted by ep 93 — our stored anchor is START 194 / {194-195}, AFG's row 93 prints '194, 195', and Toei's own ep-93 synopsis carries the same beat verbatim ('ひとり湘北での居残り特訓を言い渡された花道は、安西とマンツーマンの特訓を始める'), so this is a DUPLICATE graft, not a first-time page. Half (b) FAILS too: 'Sakuragi is assigned solo training instead of going to the camp' is a setup beat, not a death, a reveal or an arc close. Neither half holds, so the rule's plain text applies — 'A duplicate graft or a trivial first-time beat stays filler'. Row stays FILLER, no anchor (A1 + A44), and Sean's 2026-08-25 A1 deletion on this row ('pure anime-original beachside comedy episode') is confirmed. Which source lied: animefillerguide, in its class column — it blue-marks 'Mixed' and prints '194' on the strength of a ~3-minute tag, while printing '194, 195' on the very next row without partitioning the chapter; its own timestamped note ('we only watch from minute 19:14 to the end') is the disproof. AFG's chapter column here is a reading-position header, exactly as the catalog says. The stored partial{194 (opening)} annotation is kept in substance but corrected in kind (partial → graft) and given its weight and its duplicate status.

anchor_hostile.why: A1: the row is filler (confirmed by Toei's own synopsis, slamdunk.fandom's synopsis and ja-WP's naming of it as one of the series' few アニメオリジナルストーリー) — roughly 19 of ~23 minutes are the anime-original beach-house plot with no source pages. A44 independently: the closing tag quotes the opening beat of ch 194, a chapter ep 93 adapts in full (stored anchor START 194, {194-195}; AFG row 93 = '194, 195'; Toei's ep-93 synopsis carries the same beat), so the fragment is a DUPLICATE and can never be a position — anchoring it would place ep 92 at a chapter the following row already owns and would falsely claim a position gain over ep 91's END 193. Sean's 2026-08-25 A1 deletion is CONFIRMED, not re-opened.

annotations.chapters: 194 (opening beat — the camp departs, Sakuragi is held back at Anzai's request)
annotations.note: weight: SLIVER — because it runs from 19:14 to the end of a ~23-minute episode whose other ~19 minutes have no source pages (animefillerguide's own timestamp; Toei's official synopsis describes only the beach-house plot), and because the beat is not told as source narrative but repurposed as the punchline of the anime-original money story (slamdunk.fandom: Sakuragi steals the gang's earnings to fund his trip, learns he is being left behind, and the gang steal the money back). The material is a DUPLICATE, not new: ch 194 合宿 (vol 22, 21 pages) is adapted by ep 93, which carries the anchor (START 194, {194-195}), and Toei's own ep-93 synopsis restates the same beat ('ひとり湘北での居残り特訓を言い渡された花道は、安西とマンツーマンの特訓を始める') — read the chapter there. Sole-adaptation exception checked and DECLINED on BOTH halves: the pages are in another episode, and a camp-assignment setup beat is not a death, a reveal or an arc close. Replaces the stored partial{194 (opening)} fact; kind corrected partial → graft (the episode does not partially adapt a chapter it is otherwise adapting — it quotes the opening of a chapter that belongs to the next row), substance unchanged.

structure.notes: STORED TYPE CONFIRMED — no type_correction, deliberately: ep 92 stays filler and AFL is the label that got it right. PREMISE / PRIOR-VERDICT CORRECTION: the batch-20 slam-dunk verdict's structure note says 'AFL has NO page for slam-dunk (404); the AFL column in the context is AFG's data'. The 404 is only true of the guessed slug — the live page is https://www.animefillerlist.com/shows/slam-dunk-0 (linked from /shows), it holds 102 rows, and its types around the target are 88-89 Manga Canon, 90 Mixed Canon/Filler, 91 Manga Canon, 92 Filler, 93-94 Manga Canon, 95 Filler, 96 Manga Canon, 97 Filler — which matches our stored types row for row. So AFL and AFG really are two sources on this series, the context's 'AFL:' column is genuine AFL data, and the earlier note should be amended. Row identity: AFL 102 rows vs our 101 (AFL carries one extra, consistent with the two SP digests ja-WP describes between eps 21/22 and 61/62); nothing was index-joined — row 92 was matched on TITLE + DATE ('Male Friendship!? Sakuragi's Gang', 1996-01-13, exactly the context's values) with 88-97 read around it. AFG's slam-dunk table joins by title and is 101 rows. Toei's per-episode pages were keyed by number AND verified by title: /episode/92/ returns 第 92 話 男の友情!?花道軍団, /episode/93/ returns 第 93 話 2万本への挑戦, /episode/91/ returns 第 91 話 全国が危ない！ — all three match our stored titles in translation, so the licensor numbering is our numbering. Chapter space: one space — slamdunk.fandom's Chapter 194 page reads volume=22, pages=21, japanese=合宿, and our stored boundary table gives v22 = 189-197; the 276-chapter / 31-volume tankōbon numbering is used by every source here. Sources beyond the two labels: (1) Toei Animation's official 各話 pages (the licensor) for eps 91, 92, 93, 94; (2) slamdunk.fandom via the MediaWiki API — Episode 92, Episode 93, Chapter 193, Chapter 194; (3) ja-Wikipedia's SLAM DUNK article prose on the anime's original episodes. Note that slamdunk.fandom's episode infoboxes have EMPTY chapter fields ('chapter = [[Chapter |Chapter ]]-[[Chapter |Chapter ]]') across this range — that is silence, not a claim of no chapters, so the synopsis prose was used instead.
structure.coverage_set_checked: ep 90 {191-192}, ep 91 {193}, ep 92 = ch 194's opening beat only (duplicate), ep 93 {194-195}, ep 94 {196}, ep 96 {197} = the honest terminal — ch 194 is fully owned by ep 93 and nothing is stranded by typing 92 filler.

flags_for_sean: AFL confirmed, AFG refuted, and this row is the second witness in this wave to the same AFG behaviour (inuyasha 79 is the first): AFG's blue 'Mixed' class can rest on a timestamped tail of a few minutes or even one page, and the cell's own note says so. On animefillerguide, the NOTE is evidence and the CLASS is an opinion — worth adding to the agent definition, since the T4 strong-tier flag is generated from that class and will keep producing this shape.

A correction to the batch-20 slam-dunk verdict's structure note, which is now in the record: AFL DOES have a slam-dunk page — /shows/slam-dunk-0, not /shows/slam-dunk. That matters beyond this row, because the earlier note concluded 'the AFL column in the context is AFG's data', which would make AFL and AFG one lineage on this series. They are two. I did not open any other slam-dunk row.

Toei's lineup.toei-anim.co.jp per-episode synopses are alive and complete for this series (91-94 read directly, all with full あらすじ text in the page body — not in og:description, which is absent). Combined with slamdunk.fandom's empty per-episode chapter fields, the licensor text is the better instrument for this series' remaining rows; ep 93's synopsis alone settled the duplicate question here.
